'''Kolchin's problems''' are a set of [[open problem|unsolved problems]] in [[differential algebra]], outlined by [[Ellis Kolchin]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1966 [[Moscow|(Moscow)]]

== Kolchin Catenary Conjecture ==

The '''Kolchin Catenary Conjecture''' is a fundamental open problem in [[differential algebra]] related to [[dimension theory]].

===Statement===
"Let <math>\Sigma</math> be a differential [[algebraic variety]] of [[dimension]] <math>d</math>.
By a ''long gap chain'' we mean a chain of irreducible differential subvarieties <math>\Sigma_0 \subset \Sigma_1 \subset \Sigma_2 \subset \cdots</math> of [[ordinal number]] length <math>\omega^m \cdot d</math>."

Given an irreducible differential variety <math>\Sigma</math> of dimension <math>d > 0</math> and an arbitrary point <math>p \in \Sigma</math> , does there exist a long gap chain beginning at <math>p</math> and ending at <math>\Sigma</math>? 

The positive answer to this question is called the Kolchin catenary conjecture.<ref> Kolchin, Ellis Robert, Alexandru Buium, and Phyllis Joan Cassidy. Selected works of Ellis Kolchin with commentary.
